Department Marketing Statement

Student Health is a full service on campus primary healthcare facility for UCSB students. We see students on both an appointment and walk in basis. Our auxiliary services included on-site laboratory, pharmacy, and x-ray. Our specialty services include psychiatry and sports medicine.

Benefits Of Belonging

Working at UC means being part of this vibrant institution that shines a light on what is possible. People make UC great, and UC recognizes your contributions by making this a great place to work. Excellent retirement and health are just one of the rewards. Learn more about the benefits of working at UC

Brief Summary Of Job Duties

The Transitional Executive Director for Student Health / Assistant Vice Chancellor for Integrated Care (AVC/ED) provides overall strategic and operational leadership for Student Health Services (SHS), driving high-quality, cost-effective care that supports the academic mission and wellbeing of over 25,000 students. The AVC/ED manages daily operations through subordinate managers and senior directors across diverse clinical and administrative disciplines, including primary care, behavioral health, psychiatry, ancillary services, and the Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP). The position holds primary accountability for a $30+ million budget, ~100 FTE staff, regulatory compliance, risk management, and the overall financial, operational, and physical infrastructure of the health system.

Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing, this two-year executive appointment provides strategic leadership for implementing organizational improvements identified through a 2026 external review of UC Santa Barbara's Student Health Service and Behavioral Health System of Care planning process. The position leads the development of Student Health's strategic plan, and advances an integrated behavioral health model across Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services, and campus partners, and directs complex organizational change initiatives. Through executive oversight of senior leadership, strategic planning, organizational development, and financial sustainability initiatives, the incumbent is accountable for implementing a coordinated behavioral health system that improves access, care navigation, operational effectiveness, performance outcomes, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health, Healthcare Administration or related fields along with at least 10 years of relevant experience in a leadership or administrative role OR
M.D., Ph.D., Psy.D. or other clinical training along with at least five years of relevant experience in healthcare administration in a leadership role.

Preferred Qualifications

Executive Leadership role in College health care setting.
Experience with physical and psychological health care integration.

Special Conditions Of Employment

This is a two year contract position.
Mandated reporting requirements of Child Abuse
UCSB Campus Security Authority under Clery Act
Works in patient care environment
Satisfactory criminal history background check
UCSB is a Tobacco-Free environment

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement

As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.

“Misconduct” Means Any Violation Of The Policies Governing Employee Conduct At The Applicant’s Previous Place Of Employment, Including, But Not Limited To, Violations Of Policies Prohibiting Sexual Harassment, Sexual Assault, Or Other Forms Of Harassment, Or Discrimination, As Defined By The Employer. For Reference, Below Are UC’s Policies Addressing Some Forms Of Misconduct

UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy

UC Anti-Discrimination Policy

Abusive Conduct in the Workplace\

Job Functions And Percentages Of Time

30% Change Management and Organizational Transformation

Strategic Planning & Executive Governance: Directs the Student Health Service executive team in formulating multi-year strategic plans and long-term policies, establishing organizational vision and operational goals that align service delivery with campus needs, care access, and fiscal sustainability.

Operational Transformation & Process Improvement: Exercises high-level administrative authority to execute operational recommendations from the 2026 external review, establishing systems and operational controls to optimize:

Workforce Configuration: Aligning staffing models and FTE allocation with patient demand.
Provider Productivity: Formulating and monitoring daily provider encounter benchmarks.
Billing Expansion & Revenue Optimization: Directing revenue cycle infrastructure and billing team growth.
Coding Education: Overseeing clinical documentation standards and provider feedback loops.

In consultation with the AVC for Student Wellbeing, directs the ongoing rollout of broad report initiatives.

Integrated Care Model Leadership: Provides executive oversight and program evaluation for the large-scale integration and transformation of behavioral health services spanning Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS), and campus-wide wellbeing programs. Establishes executive priorities, institutional policy, and implementation frameworks across the Wellbeing Cluster to advance an operationalized, student-centered behavioral health system of care.

Change Management & Organizational Alignment: Directs executive change management strategies and organizational design frameworks to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, inter-departmental alignment, and broad adoption of modernized operating models.

Senior Leadership Advisory: Advises Wellbeing Cluster leadership and campus executives on complex, high-stakes organizational change initiatives, ensuring strict compliance with regulatory mandates, risk management standards, and strategic campus priorities.

Resource & Infrastructure Stewardship: Directs the operational, human resource, and financial infrastructure across the cluster, aligning multi-million-dollar budgets and staffing strategies to sustain the integrated health model.

Special Executive Projects: Performs other high-level healthcare administration and policy duties as assigned by the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing.

50% Operational & Strategic Leadership

Strategic Adaptation & Program Evaluation: Analyzes, evaluates, and adapts Student Health Service through subordinate leadership to respond to evolving student healthcare needs, public health challenges, accreditation and licensing requirements, and funding landscapes.

Strategic Planning & Policy Execution: Formulates and executes strategic action plans, establishing the vision, long-term goals, and operational policies needed to address emerging campus health priorities.

Financial Oversight & Resource Optimization: Monitors and directs financial management, healthcare utilization, cost-containment strategies, and overall organizational design for a large, complex health department to ensure long-term fiscal sustainability.

Comprehensive Care Delivery: Holds executive accountability for the delivery of high-quality, accessible primary, behavioral, and ancillary healthcare services to students by organizing and leveraging integrated on- and off-campus health resources. UC SHIP Governance: Exercises executive responsibility for the oversight, financial design, and utilization of the UC Student Health Insurance Plan (UC SHIP), collaborating with local leadership and actively representing the campus on UC Systemwide Advisory Boards and Implementation Teams.

UC Systemwide Alignment & Collaboration: Collaborates with peer UC Student Health Directors to coordinate cross-campus care models, monitor systemwide costs, arrange care reciprocity, and influence university-wide health policies.

Public Relations & Institutional Integrity: Maintains institutional integrity, protects organizational reputation, and leads public health messaging by serving as the approved authority for campus communications, media requests, and community relations.

20% Resource Management

Fiscal Leadership & Budgetary Control: Accountable for managing a $30+ million budget derived from complex, multi-source funding models; leads the preparation, advocacy, and strategic management of short- and long-term financial plans to ensure long-term organizational viability.

Revenue Optimization & Strategic Analysis: Directs the strategic analysis and development of revenue-generating initiatives across Student Health Service and Counseling & Psychological Services, including third-party billing models, behavioral health reimbursement expansion, and clinic operations.

Workforce Strategy & Personnel Management: Directs overarching human resources strategy and workforce planning to adapt to changing operational demands; oversees through subordinate leadership the recruitment, selection, development, and retention of staff in accordance with UC policies and affirmative action goals.

Executive Oversight & Direct Supervision: Manages daily health system operations through the Student Health Management team, providing direct supervision and executive direction to the SHS Interim Director and the Director of Billing and Revenue Cycle.

HR Governance & Labor Relations Compliance: Maintains final departmental authority for SHS human resources decisions, working in close coordination with Student Affairs, HR, and Labor Relations to ensure strict policy adherence and contract compliance across five represented bargaining units.

jobs.description:
Iridium is an award-winning and innovative satellite communications company with bragging rights to the only network that offers voice and data connectivity anywhere in the world. For over 20 years, Iridium’s unique network and services have supported critical communications needs for individuals, businesses, and the evolving Internet of Things.

At Iridium, we understand the importance of staying connected and the limitations of traditional communications networks. People across the globe, including first responders, humanitarians, global militaries, scientific researchers, and lone workers, as well as ships, aircraft and remote operations all rely on Iridium to stay connected. We take our responsibility for providing these essential communications very seriously and pride ourselves on offering a reliable lifeline when needed. Likewise, Iridium is committed to providing an exciting and innovative workplace, where employees are challenged to think outside the box and collaborate on new, bold ideas and solutions. Our talented teams are passionate about their work and the impact our company makes around the world. Iridium fosters an empowering and inclusive culture that allows employees to genuinely be their best selves. We are looking for others who want to join this truly unique company that celebrates our employees and provides the opportunity to truly make a difference in the world.

What We’re Looking For:

If you have deep experience operating within the Big Tech ecosystem and leading strategic, high‑value partnerships with hyperscalers and OEMs, you will be excited about the Executive Director, Hyperscaler & OEM Partnerships role with Iridium. In this position, you will drive execution of Authentic’s OEM integration strategy across Google, Apple, Samsung, Qualcomm, AWS, Microsoft, and others, ensuring corporate objectives and growth milestones are achieved. Your main focus will be to identify and advance a suite of Authentic solutions and initiatives from POC to full production integration and replicate this model across additional partners. You’ll bring passion for building executive relationships, negotiating complex platform‑level agreements, and shaping how next‑generation devices adopt satellite connectivity.

What You’ll Do:

Identify and promote different use cases for partnership with the entities listed above
Foster and develop a highly effective cross functional engagement model between Iridium/Authentic leadership, engineering, product, and hyperscaler/OEM executive stakeholders to accelerate partnership outcomes
Lead end to end strategic relationships with Google (Android/Pixel), Apple, Samsung, and Qualcomm at VP/SVP and C suite levels, serving as the primary executive interface, and promote integration of the Authentic solution in standard user devices
Direct the different possible use cases through POC validation, production scoping, commercial negotiation, and final contract execution
Inform decision making on commercial frameworks including revenue share models, licensing structures, and SLA commitments to support scalable OEM adoption
Coordinate engineering, technical validation, and integration planning between partner engineering teams and Authentic's product and engineering groups
Develop strategic business cases that articulate OEM ecosystem value, presenting internally and directly to partner C-suite executives to drive alignment and sponsorship
Drive repeatable integration motions across OEMs, establishing processes, templates, and governance models for future hyperscaler and chipset partnerships
Inform product development and management efforts with insights and intelligence on pain points and market requirements
Ensure clear reporting of pipeline status, deal milestones, and risk assessments directly to the Authentic GM and Iridium senior leadership
Represent Authentic at industry events, executive summits, and partner briefings, serving as a senior ambassador for Iridium's satellite connectivity strategy

What You’ll Need to Succeed:

Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, or related field OR equivalent relevant experience in lieu of degree
15+ years of relevant experience in the technology ecosystem and cybersecurity industry
Established high-level connections and networks within the targe partner ecosystem
Ability to interface with the management teams of the target partners at all levels, from senior roles to junior roles, business to technical
Able to understand and simplify complex and vague concepts, confidently drive executive discussions, make high impact decisions, and respond to difficult or ambiguous situations
Ability to work independently and to focus on achieving results
Previous management experience
Capable of being a strong motivator and source of direction for your team and exemplifying commitment to the company's goals
Excellent leadership qualities and the ability to hold yourself and others accountable for strategic outcomes
A strategic mindset and the ability to facilitate collaboration across multiple departments and external executive stakeholders
Skills needed to tackle complex challenges head on, including negotiating multi-party commercial and technical agreements
Actively looks for growth opportunities to improve how partnerships and integrations are executed

Things That Would be Great if You Brought to the Table:

Experience working at Google, Apple, Samsung, or Qualcomm in a connectivity, hardware, or OEM partnership capacity
Familiarity with satellite and PNT solutions
Background supporting high growth startup initiatives or internal venture teams
Technical fluency in modem architecture, APIs, or connectivity standards

We’ll also need you to:

Be able to work in the office at least 3 or more days a week to foster collaboration with the team and stakeholders
Be able to travel up to 40%
This position directly performs under, supports, or is exposed to a U.S. government contract. To comply with the requirements of that U.S. government contract, applicants for this position must be U.S. citizen

Work Environment:

This position primarily works in an office setting and is largely sedentary with the majority of the position working with a computer. The role typically requires the use of basic office equipment such as a phone, video, computer, keyboard, mouse, and printer.

We believe in-person connection drives innovation, strengthens mentorship, and builds culture, while flexibility enables employees to do their best work. Under Iridium’s Hybrid Work Policy, employees are expected to work at least three days per week (approximately 60%) in an Iridium office to support collaboration, relationship-building, and professional growth.

Additional Information

This job description outlines the general nature and level of work for this role and is not a comprehensive list of duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Employees may be assigned additional responsibilities as needed.

Base Pay Range: $280,000 - $335,000 USD

Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors and this range represents an estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Base salary is only one part of our compensation package for this role. You may also be eligible for company stock and annual bonus. Employee benefits also include medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage; 401(k) retirement plan options; paid time off and paid holidays; paid parental leave; and other discounts and perks.

Formed in 2025, the Florida Cooperative of Theological Schools (FCTS) aims to strengthen theological education and ministry formation in South Florida by resourcing schools and programs accredited by the Association of Theological Schools (ATS) and related entities. The Deputy Director, Digital Advertising and Marketing will play a vital role in our digital fundraising strategy, with an emphasis on overseeing revenue generation, advocacy lead recruitment, brand awareness building and donor acquisition through an integrated digital advertising program.

The ideal candidate will combine strong nonprofit leadership and administrative skills with a genuine appreciation for the arts and a commitment to making the museum welcoming, accessible, and relevant to the community. Identify grant opportunities and manage applications, reporting, and compliance.

Ensure effective promotion of exhibitions, programs, fundraising initiatives, and organizational news.

They will also demonstrate a proficiency in achieving results in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, while balancing short- and long-term organizational priorities. They are comfortable with creating revenue projections and swiftly managing budget changes on a weekly/monthly basis to achieve the highest monetary impact. Collaborative

Rawls Museum Arts, founded in 1958, is an educational and cultural institution located in the town of Courtland, Virginia. The museum offers a diverse gallery calendar showcasing a wide range of artists and is free and open to the public, making art accessible to all community members. In addition to exhibitions, Rawls Museum Arts provides classes that support local artists in exploring new mediums and developing their specialties. The museum is a community hub for artistic engagement, learning, and cultural enrichment.

Role Description:

Rawls Museum Arts is seeking a dedicated, community-minded Executive Director to provide leadership for the museum’s artistic, educational, operational, financial, and community programs. The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, artists, donors, community partners, and patrons to advance the museum’s mission and strengthen its role as a cultural resource for Courtland, Southampton County, and the surrounding region.

The ideal candidate will combine strong nonprofit leadership and administrative skills with a genuine appreciation for the arts and a commitment to making the museum welcoming, accessible, and relevant to the community. As the museum’s primary ambassador and public representative, the Executive Director will provide organizational leadership while overseeing programs, exhibitions, financial management, fundraising, communications, and day-to-day operations.

Leadership and Strategic Planning

Provide overall leadership and day-to-day management of Rawls Museum Arts.
Work with the Board of Directors to develop, implement, and evaluate strategic goals, policies, and organizational priorities.
Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative of the museum at community events, meetings, presentations, and other public engagements.
Build strong relationships with community organizations, leaders, and other partners.
Develop organizational plans and evaluate programs and operations to identify opportunities for growth, improvement, and long-term sustainability.

Exhibitions and Programs

Oversee and participate in the planning, development, and presentation of exhibitions, community programs, and special events.
Provide organizational oversight of educational programming in collaboration with staff.
Develop relationships with artists, instructors, performers, and cultural partners and support programming that reflects the interests and needs of the community.
Evaluate program participation and community response to inform future programming.

Fundraising and Development

Lead efforts to secure support through grants, sponsorships, memberships, individual giving, fundraising events, and other development initiatives.
Cultivate and maintain relationships with donors, sponsors, members, funders, and supporters.
Work with the Board to establish fundraising strategies and annual development goals.
Identify grant opportunities and manage applications, reporting, and compliance.

Financial and Administrative Management

Manage the museum’s annual budget, financial operations, accounting, and fiscal priorities in collaboration with the Board and appropriate financial professionals.
Maintain accurate financial records and monitor income, expenses, and financial activity.
Ensure compliance with nonprofit requirements, policies, contracts, and grant obligations.
Oversee facilities, purchasing, vendors, insurance, administrative systems, Gift Shop operations, and other day-to-day needs.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Supervise, support, and evaluate staff and contractors and provide clear direction and priorities.
Identify staffing needs and support the recruitment, training, and development of staff and volunteers.
Foster a positive, inclusive, collaborative, and professional organizational culture.

Marketing and Communications

Develop and oversee marketing and communications strategy in collaboration with staff.
Ensure effective promotion of exhibitions, programs, fundraising initiatives, and organizational news.
Develop and maintain relationships with regional media and support effective public relations.

Board and Governance

Work closely with the Board of Directors and committees to support effective governance and advance the museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Prepare reports and other materials for Board and committee meetings and keep the Board informed of significant organizational activities, challenges, and opportunities.
Implement Board-approved policies and initiatives and provide recommendations regarding organizational needs and opportunities.

Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Ability to manage budgets and financial responsibilities, and prioritize competing responsibilities.
Proficiency with or ability to quickly learn financial, database, website, communications, and other administrative software and systems.

Ability to work evening and weekend events.
Experience supervising staff, contractors, and/or volunteers.
